_comment: Marius's training: One-handed and Block to 75 (Expert), Two-handed, Light and Heavy Armor to 50 (Journeyman), no master levels; gold at vanilla's price; Guild members only. The texts come from drafting/marius_approved.json. npcgen builds a top-level choice 'ask' with Marius's reply 'reply' (voiced), then one choice per skill; a skill's reply is his recorded 'Of course.' (pick) and runs AGHallTrainerTIF, which sets the skill and cap on his class (AG_Native.SetTrainerSkill) and opens vanilla's training menu. 'skill' is vanilla's CLAS skill index (0 One-handed, 1 Two-handed, 3 Block, 5 Heavy Armor, 6 Light Armor).
reply: Aye, I can. It'll cost you same as any trainer... I'm just able to teach you more things.
_pick: Each skill's reply (a recorded vanilla line that fits): his vanilla 'Of course.' take, copied; then the menu opens.
_watch: Marius's idles while he watches practice (drafting/marius_training_approved.json): said to himself at his post (within 'near' of AGHallTrainWatchMarker), only while a trainee in that pool runs a practice package: melee = the 'train' packages (Ghrulek, Zhasim, Caralion at the dummies), archery = the 'archery' packages (Nessa, Ylva at the targets). Ahead of his own idles in the idle topic; 'chance' is each line's percent per idle check, 'reset' the game hours before a line can play again (the hall's idles have 1, which suits pools that run all day, not a three-hour practice). 'ids' gives each line its ID by its place (merged 0x9A40 on), so the voice files keep their names: append a new line there, never reorder. The pools' order is the INFO order within each pool.

melee.trainMelee13: Knees bent. You fight from the ground up.
melee.trainMelee11: Breathe out when you strike. Not in.
melee.trainMelee10: Slower. Get it right first, then get it fast.
melee.trainMelee6: Not bad. Now do it again with a feint.
melee.trainMelee15: Where's your back foot? Find it.
melee.trainMelee42: Never expect them to drop from the first blow. Follow it up.
melee.trainMelee48: Neck, armpit, back of the knee. That's where the gaps are.
melee.trainMelee49: Treat that dummy like it brought friends.
melee.trainMelee57: Loose grip on the swing. Squeeze as it lands.
melee.trainMelee52: Again, but mean it this time. Get lazy in here and someone buries you out there.
melee.trainMelee60: Good. Now let's change it up. I want you to add a parry and riposte after your first strike.

archery.trainArchery3: Don't admire the shot. Nock the next one.
archery.trainArchery11: Same draw, every time. Breathe, release, and repeat until perfect.
archery.trainArchery22: That one's a kill. Make every one look like it.
archery.trainArchery23: Better. Keep your bow arm still after the release.
archery.trainArchery30: Elbow up on the draw. Don't let it sag.
archery.trainArchery42: A good archer saved more of us than any shield. Let's focus on consecutive quick shots next.
